children: Tariffs Canada will impose in retaliation for new U.S. levies will help some industries but hurt most and weaken economic growth by raising costs for producers and consumers, Oxford Economics argues. And Oxford's analysis suggests fiscal relief planned by Ottawa will briefly soften the economic impact of the Trump administration's tariffs but won't offset the overall drag from bilateral levies. It says paper, wood, steel, and aluminum product manufacturers will see the largest marginal benefit from Canadian counter-tariffs, since they will reduce U.S. imports and encourage substitution toward domestic production. But Oxford adds nearly all Canadian manufacturers will feel net negative impacts from the bilateral tariff escalation.(robb.stewart@wsj.com; @RobbMStewart)
